ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as substantially amended by the Law of 13 January 2019 implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 in respect of the central Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); associated Grand-Ducal Regulations and CSSF Regulations/Regulatory Circulars, including CSSF Regulation 12-02 on professional obligations and CSSF AML/CFT supervisory circulars.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers or equivalent foreign official registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the foreign registry is in a Hague Convention Signatory State)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of constitution (acte de constitution) of the SCSp including the partnership agreement (contrat de société)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial deed registered and recorded at the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (no apostille required for domestic legal effect; originals issued with notarial authenticity)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (attestation de dépôt des comptes / compliance certificate) of each foreign corporate general partner and limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent foreign registrar or tax authority in the partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, absent apostille coverage, Luxembourg consular legalization in the State of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified sworn translation into French of all non-English and non-French corporate resolutions, powers of attorney and partnership documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-recognized sworn translator / Ministry of Justice approved translator in Luxembourg or in the State of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization of the translator's certification where required by Luxembourg registry practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized declaration of acceptance of office by general partner (associé commandité) and of registered office collocation consent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all natural person UBOs, general partners and limited partners against the Luxembourg national PEP repository, EU consolidated sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, FATF public statements and high-risk jurisdiction lists, and CSSF AML/CFT sanction and embargo guidance. Immediate enhanced due diligence is required for any political person, state-owned counterparty, or transaction involving a jurisdiction subject to Union restrictive measures; systems must be capable of continuous screening and audit-trail generation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal — www.lbr.lu (official register: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script; non-Latin names must be transliterated into the appropriate statute-accepted phonetic form. The legal form suffix must be written as 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' in the registered name. Names may be in French, German, Luxembourgish, English, or another modern language using Latin characters, provided the RCS can establish distinctiveness and transliteration compliance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written, reasoned motion for reconsideration with the Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 days of notification, accompanied by supporting legal arguments and alternative name submissions. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may lodge an administrative appeal to the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of the rejection decision; during the appeal, the rejected name may not be used and the priority date is lost unless interim relief preserving the priority is granted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual registered office is not accepted for an entity conducting regulated contract research organization activities within Luxembourg. The SCSp may lawfully use a registered-office service provider for administrative seat purposes when it functions as a pure investment/finance vehicle, but for a clinical trial CRO the Luxembourg Ministry of Health and competent professional regulators require a meaningful physical operational presence, including record retention, pharmacovigilance, quality assurance and trial management premises, sufficient personnel, and actual business substance. A virtual address alone will be challenged in both commercial register formalities and any regulatory licensing inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30% to 40% quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 18 months of operation, given the regulated clinical-trial environment and the Luxembourg AML/CFT supervisory authorities' focus on economic substance of partnership vehicles.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended, comprising the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013; applicable provisions on partnership formation, liability of limited partners, and mandatory registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), together with the implementing Grand-Ducal regulations on the trade and companies register.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration (demande d'immatriculation) filed electronically through the LBR e-Registration portal, accompanied by the executed partnership agreement (contrat de société / acte constitutif), appointment documents of the general partner (gérant), and the registered office or domiciliation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement for an SCSp; the partnership agreement freely sets the subscribed capital, which may be zero or in kind, and any paid-in capital must simply be contributed per the deed. No capital deposit into a blocked escrow account is required under Luxembourg law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the capital contributions of each partner in the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) are hereby approved as fully subscribed in accordance with the executed partnership agreement.

FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp is hereby established at [Registered Office Address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.

FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name of General Partner / Gérant] is appointed manager (gérant) of the SCSp with full powers to represent the partnership, to open bank accounts, to appoint service providers, and to complete all filings with the Luxembourg Business Registers.

FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed initial compliance officer responsible for regulatory filings, statutory records, and clinical-trial licensing coordination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (if real property is contributed or elective notarization) or the partners directly in a private deed; no mandatory notarization for a standard SCSp formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in French, German, or English, identifying the name of the partnership, its legal form 'Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp)', the registered office address, the duration (maximum 30 years unless extended), the contributions of each commandité and commanditaire, and the powers of the general partner-gérant. Have all partners and the gérant sign the deed; if any contribution consists of real property, execute before a Luxembourg notary and register the deed. Obtain a sworn translation in the language of the RCS form if the deed was drafted in a non-French, non-German, or non-English language.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national identity card of each partner and of the general partner (gérant)
Proof of residential address for each partner (utility bill or bank statement less than 3 months old)
Tax identification number (TIN) of each partner and the gérant
Draft SCSp partnership agreement containing the statutory particulars
Sworn translation of the deed (if drafted in any language other than French, German, or English)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries any clause of the deed or the accompanying documents, the partners may execute a curative amendment deed (acte rectificatif) or provide supplemental legal explanations through counsel; resubmission is processed via the same RCS window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration of the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS e-Registration service (www.lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed partnership agreement and all mandatory attachments through the LBR e-Registration portal within one month of execution. Complete the RCS registration form indicating the legal form (SCSp), the name, registered office, object (clinical trial research management services), duration, managers, and powers of the gérant. Settle the €75 registration fee online and upload the proof of payment. Upon approval, obtain the RCS incorporation extract (extrait) and the national business identification number (numéro d'immatriculation).
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (notarized or private) in PDF
RCS registration request form (formulaire d'immatriculation)
Certified copy of the partners' resolution appointing the gérant and compliance officer
Domiciliation agreement from the registered office provider (if the office is provided by a domiciliation agent)
Written acceptance of office by the gérant (if not included in the deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where a query is raised by the RCS registrar, respond within 1 month through the LBR secure messaging system with corrected documents; in case of refusal, appeal to the District Court of Luxembourg sitting in commercial matters within the statutory limitation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration – direct taxes, VAT, municipal business tax, and beneficial ownership filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); beneficial ownership register administered by the LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the RCS extract and file the tax registration with the AEDT for value added tax (VAT) using form 010 if the SCSp will supply taxable services in Luxembourg, and with the ACD for the municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and for tax-assessment purposes. Although the SCSp is tax-transparent, it must nonetheless hold a business identification number and file annual partnership statements. File the declaration of beneficial owners (RBE declaration) with the LBR within 30 days of registration, identifying each natural person ultimately owning or controlling 25% or more of the partnership.
required_dossiers: RCS incorporation extract
VAT registration form 010 (déclaration d'inscription à la TVA)
SCSp partnership agreement
Identity documents and TIN of the general partner and any tax agent
Beneficial ownership register filing (RBE form) with the LBR
Bank account details of the partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration requires additional data, respond within the time limit indicated in the request; any refusal to register for tax purposes may be contested by an appeal to the Director of the AEDT or ACD within 3 months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a Luxembourg corporate bank account and funding of agreed capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed Luxembourg credit institution (bank) supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the RCS extract, deed, UBO register confirmation, and business plan to the bank's corporate desk and complete the KYC/KYS documentation demonstrating the economic purpose of clinical-trial management services. The bank will conduct an AML risk assessment (the service is classified as standard low risk under the Luxembourg AML/CFT regime). Transfer the agreed subscribed capital (if any) into the partnership's account; for SCSp the account may be held in the partnership's name.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt and current photographic IDs of all authorized signatories and UBOs
SCSp partnership agreement and pro-forma resolution excerpts
UBO declaration confirmation or a signed UBO structure chart
Business plan describing the CRO activities and expected turnovers
Proof of address (domiciliation certificate) and corporate constitutions of any corporate partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If additional due diligence is required, provide enhanced documentation (source of funds, statutory financial statements, bank references); if the bank still declines, file a complaint with CSSF or open the account at another licensed institution—referral to a specialist cross-border desk is the preferred cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration with the Luxembourg social security administration (CCSS) and occupational health setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) and the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp as an employer on the CCSS portal (e-Sécurité social) before the first employee start date, filing the employer declaration and the conformity certificate. Obtain the employer number and align payroll contributions (social security, dependency insurance) with the CCSS schedule. If the SCSp maintains an office or laboratory, notify ITM for the occupational safety inventory, arrange a medical assessment of staff, and ensure workstation compliance with applicable codes.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and national identification number of the SCSp
Employer registration form (SM/DEC) with list of initial directors/managers and employees
Copy of employment contracts or planned staffing chart
Domiciliation certificate or lease of the Luxembourg office
ITM occupational risk assessment form (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or queried, file the missing employee and activity data via the e-Sécurité portal with retroactive effect where permitted; contest CCSS decisions before the social security arbitration body and align employer payments to avoid late-interest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health – Direction de la Santé, Division of Pharmacy and Medicines, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Authorisation for the conduct of clinical trials on medicinal products for human use and/or registration of a contract research organisation (CRO) engaged in trial management, under the Luxembourg Law of 17 April 2008 (and Regulation (EU) No 536/2014), together with any business licence (autorisation d'établissement) required under the Law of 2 September 2011 for regulated professional services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Agency (Administration de l'environnement), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based CRO management activity without an EU Industrial Emissions Directive installation threshold; a simplified environmental declaration may become necessary if a bioanalytical or biobanking laboratory is established
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater into public sewers must meet the municipal discharge by-law and EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (Directive 91/271/EEC) parameter limits; VOC emissions remain under the de minimis threshold of the Solvent Emissions Directive (Directive 1999/13/EC) for office/laboratory use; clinical trial waste, including pharmaceutical samples, is classified as medical/hazardous waste and must be removed by a licensed waste operator under the Law of 21 March 2012 and EU Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 labelling rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) confirming fire extinguisher coverage, evacuation routes, and alarm systems; municipal building occupancy certificate from the competent commune verifying structural load-bearing safety, electrical safety, and fire compartmentation; occupational clearance from the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (ITM) under the Luxembourg Labour Code provisions on workers' safety and health, including first-aid equipment, ergonomic workstations, and, for any laboratory, biological safety containment review.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Inland Revenue (direct taxes) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) - indirect taxes and VAT. Official portals: guichet.lu (single administrative portal), the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) e-portal, MyGuichet/AED e-filing for VAT matters, and Luxembourg Customs (Administration des douanes et accises) for EU ECS export clearances.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Incorporate the SCSp before a Luxembourg notary and register with the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Societes) via guichet.lu; the RCS issues the sole legal-entity identifier (matricule, i.e., the Business Registration Number). STEP 2: The ACD assigns the national tax identification number (NIF, numéro d'identification) on registration or at the first tax filing; this number is used for all direct-tax filings and correspondence with the ACD. STEP 3: Register for VAT with the AED by submitting the electronic start-of-activity and VAT registration form through MyGuichet; the AED allocates a Luxembourg VAT number with the prefix 'LU' plus 8 digits. An SCSp, although civilly transparent, is itself a separate taxable person for VAT purposes when it carries on an economic activity; VAT grouping remains available where the conditions are met. STEP 4: If the CRO will physically export investigational medicinal products or trial supplies, obtain an EORI number (prefix 'LU') from Luxembourg Customs and enrol in the EU Export Control System (ECS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box election. The SCSp, created by the Law of 12 July 2013, is a partnership without legal personality and is fiscally transparent: under the general transparency rule of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (Article 175 LIR), no entity-level corporate income tax is levied; each partner is taxed directly on its allocable share of the CRO's profits at its own corporate or personal tax rate, subject to specific net wealth tax considerations affecting the SCSp. No domestic election exists to convert the SCSp into an opaque corporation. For cross-border CRO groups, maintain consistent classification between Luxembourg and the residence states of the partners to avoid hybrid mismatches; the ATAD anti-hybrid rules (implemented by the Law of 21 December 2018) may disallow deductions if a foreign jurisdiction treats the SCSp as opaque. Accordingly, the partnership deed, the Luxembourg tax classification, and the arm's-length remuneration of the general partner should be documented and consistently applied.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) - Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 implementing Directive 2006/112/EC (EU VAT Directive)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) under the small-enterprise exemption of Article 57 of the VAT Law, available only to businesses established in Luxembourg. Non-established foreign businesses have no exemption threshold and must register with the AED from the first taxable transaction; businesses established outside the EU generally must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative. The CRO's milestone fee pattern will almost always exceed the threshold, so mandatory Luxembourg VAT registration is the working assumption, together with reverse-charge or local VAT registration in host states where trial services are physically performed.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mechanism. E-invoicing follows the EU Peppol standard; B2G e-invoicing is mandatory for suppliers to the central public purchasing agency (SIM) through the national eFact/eFaktur platform. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary, but VAT invoices must be issued within 15 days of the taxable event and must satisfy the statutory EU VAT-invoice requirements. Intra-EU B2B supplies are reported via recapitulative statements, periodic VAT returns (Form 1030) are filed electronically with the AED on a monthly or quarterly basis, and export clearances are lodged electronically in the EU ECS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods (investigational medicinal products, biological specimens, medical devices, and trial supplies) to destinations outside the EU qualify for the 0% export rate under Article 49 of the Luxembourg VAT Law (Article 146 of Directive 2006/112/EC) when the goods are dispatched or transported out of the EU and the supplier holds proof of export satisfactory to the AED. CRO and clinical-trial management services (protocol design, data management, regulatory support, trial monitoring, and site-management fees) supplied to a non-EU business customer fall outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the general B2B place-of-supply rule (customer-location rule), producing an economically zero-rated outcome, provided the third-country establishment of the recipient and the business character of the supply are documented; services actually performed at an EU location may fall under different place-of-supply rules and must be analysed on a contract-by-contract basis. Intra-EU B2B supplies are subject to reverse charge in the customer's member state, requiring the client's valid EU VAT identification and recapitulative statement reporting.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration (ECS) lodged with Luxembourg Customs and validated with the export status and supervising-office clearance
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note showing physical departure of the goods from the EU to the third-country destination
Commercial invoice and packing list referencing the third-country consignee, the LU VAT number, and the underlying export contract
Inward remittance certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank confirmation evidencing receipt of the export consideration from abroad (FX repatriation evidence)
Transport evidence: delivery notes, terminal receipts, carrier contracts, and proof of arrival in the destination country
Customer status evidence: valid EU VAT ID for intra-EU reverse charge, or for non-EU clients written confirmation of third-country business establishment, plus the EC Sales List where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED may audit export evidence during the five-year statutory assessment period and retrospectively reclassify a zero-rated claim as taxable in Luxembourg if the documentation is missing, defective, or internally inconsistent; the VAT is then reassessed at the standard rate (16%) together with statutory late-payment interest. Administrative fines of up to EUR 25,000 apply under the VAT Law for documentation or filing failures, and the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung) imposes additional penalties and interest for negligence or wilful evasion, including personal liability of the SCSp's general partner and managers. Fabrication of export documents constitutes criminal tax fraud punishable by fines and imprisonment under Luxembourg criminal law, and goods that disappear within the EU may trigger joint and several liability under the customs-status rules. Services improperly excluded from Luxembourg VAT on inadequate B2B evidence are clawed back in the same manner, with penalties accruing daily. Luxembourg does not impose a separate statutory FX-repatriation deadline, but completing inward remittances within the 180-day reference window demonstrates commercial creditworthiness, supports the transfer-pricing file, and aligns with standard banking AML/KYC monitoring for the Clinical-Trial CRO payment rails.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking, AML/CFT, and prudential supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full member of the Economic and Monetary Union; the euro is fully convertible on both capital and current account transactions. No exchange control authorization is required for foreign direct investment, portfolio investment, dividend distributions, interest payments, license fees, or profit repatriation. Capital transfers are unrestricted subject to EU sanctions regulations, anti-money laundering checks, and BCL statistical reporting thresholds. Profit remittance by an SCSp is taxed at the partner level and freely distributable without any approval, provided the general partner demonstrates beneficial ownership and compliance with substance requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg does not impose any export proceeds surrender rules, mandatory conversion ratios, or holding-period requirements. Exporters and service providers may retain receipts in any currency and are free to convert to EUR at market rates. The only administrative obligation is the statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL for certain gross cross-border payment flows, typically captured by the banking counterparty via prescribed purpose codes; this is not a treasury constraint but a compliance-census exercise.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Current Account and Capital Contributions Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Clinical Trial Milestone Escrow

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions or payment institutions (e.g., fully CSSF-licensed EMIs) may provide IBAN accounts and multi-currency wallets, but they frequently restrict use to simple pass-through payments and rarely support SCSp capital escrow or clinical trial milestone segregation. Non-EEA digital EMIs operating without an EU passport cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to a Luxembourg SCSp; any such onboarding would create regulatory and tax-nexus risk. For a clinical trial CRO management vehicle, a tier-1 commercial bank remains the defensive default; an EMI may be used only for low-value ancillary operational expenses and must have robust AML frameworks in place.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks, under CSSF Circular 19/741 and law of 12 November 2004 (AML/CFT), require the general partner and all authorized signatories of the SCSp to complete a full KYC dossier. A physical appearance at the bank's Luxembourg offices is standard for partnerships with offshore GP structures or any non-EEA ultimate beneficial owner; remote video onboarding can be accepted only when strong electronic identification (eIDAS-compliant eID) and supplementary documentary verification are available. For the low-risk clinical trial CRO sponsor relationship, a hybrid protocol is common: remote video identification for the capital contributor and one in-person constitutional interview for the general partner. The bank will require proof of the SCSp's RCS registration, the limited partnership agreement, and evidence of beneficial ownership of every natural person holding more than 10% of capital or control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity around the SCSp's chain of Limited Partners (LPs) or use of a corporate general partner that is not independently managed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Latvian/global corporate registry extracts (RCS Luxembourg, Trade Register), certified organizational chart, full LP register signed by the GP, notarized resolutions, sourcing of funds for capital commitments, and a legal opinion from a Luxembourg counsel confirming the economic and beneficial ownership profile; include a prominence declaration for each natural person holding >10%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared clinical trial invoices and treasury flows, especially milestone payments scheduled across different jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed CRO master services agreement, detailed clinical trial budget with milestone triggers, each corresponding commercial invoice, sponsor purchase orders, protocol and patient recruitment master schedules, and bank statements demonstrating the synchronized cash movement; define the funds flow map and expected transaction frequency in the initial onboarding questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions exposure or PEP linkage to trial sponsors, clinical sites, or CRO subcontractors in restricted jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanctions screening across EU, OFAC, UN, and UK lists; comprehensive negative news intelligence; external legal opinion certifying that no trial site or sponsor is sanctioned; contractual indemnities and representations from the trial sponsor; evidence of only incidental non-sanctioned-country counter-party relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of physical substance or taxable operational presence in Luxembourg for the SCSp.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement, clinical trial project-management office evidence, payroll for a Luxembourg-based project manager or CRO functions, board minutes of the GP demonstrating Luxembourg decision-making, and a substance file showing that treasury, invoicing, and compliance duties are performed in Luxembourg.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity and debt capital injections into the SCSp from non-resident sponsors are routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 (for bank-to-bank credit) using the harmonized BCL balance-of-payments purpose code for Direct Investment – Equity Capital; where the injection is a shareholder loan, use the code for Intra-Group Lending/Financial Intercompany Loan. The bank will require the underlying legal documentation (capital commitment deed, subscription agreement, promissory contribution certificate) and will verify the source of funds against the UBO declarations. TARGET2 is used for EUR settlement; for non-EUR injections, the bank will apply the euro conversion at the prevailing market rate with full source tax / withholding tax screening. The SCSp must not receive crypto-asset transfers or unbanked bearer instruments; only cleared bank wires or SEPA direct credits from the accurately identified sponsor are acceptable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Treasury disbursements for clinical trial site payments, CRO subcontractors, laboratory fees, patient compensation, and insurance premiums are executed predominantly by SEPA Instant (for EUR within EU) and SWIFT MT103 (ISO 20022 CBPR+) for non-EUR and high-value transactions. All disbursement instructions must contain an actionable purpose code and the counterparty's valid bank identifier; KYC files for each beneficiary are pre-validated to prevent money-laundering red flags. For large milestones exceeding EUR 500,000, a documentary credit (standby/commercial LC via SWIFT MT700/MT760) is prudent to provide settlement certainty against clinical trial deliverables; invoices, shipment proof of diagnostic materials, and milestone completion certificates must be presented. The central liquidity clearing rail is TARGET2 for euro leg and a mix of SWIFT AGN and CHIPS for USD/GBP legs, with reconciliation performed through the SCSp's single treasury booking platform.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (where material long-term debt exists)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) only for counterpart currencies with non-convertible or illiquid markets; not standard for EUR
Currency Swaps (FX swaps) for intra-trial working capital management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RBE beneficial-owner confirmation for the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of initial RBE registration; any transfer or change of partnership interests must be declared within one month of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 125–250 (approx. USD 134–267); continued non-compliance may lead to criminal fines, judicial enforcement, and, after persistent default over three years, court-ordered strike-off from the Luxembourg RCS register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing for entities subject to mandatory publication (conditional for SCSp; not automatic unless a general partner is a legal entity or the partnership exceeds small-company thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS and Recueil électronique des sociétés (RES)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by partners within six months after financial year-end and deposited within one month of approval; for a calendar-year SCSp, final deposit deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines from EUR 500 to EUR 5,000 (approx. USD 535–5,340) for late or defective filing; interested parties or the public prosecutor may petition the tribunal de commerce to compel filing; three consecutive years of default may trigger judicial dissolution and strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual enterprise data confirmation to the Central Business Register (STATEC declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: STATEC – Central Business Register of Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 28 February, or as notified by STATEC, for data relating to the preceding calendar year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Luxembourg statistics law up to EUR 500 (approx. USD 535); repeated failure to file may lead to formal court summons and suspension of access to certain LBR administrative filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of continued compliance with the commercial establishment licence for clinical-trial CRO services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale de l'autorisation d'établissement (DGAE); clinical-trial activities also under Ministry of Health (Direction de la Santé)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the annual anniversary of issuance of the establishment authorisation; any change in managers, partners, registered office, or activity scope must be notified within 15 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without, or outside the scope of, a valid authorisation is a criminal offence with fines of EUR 1,000 to EUR 25,000 (approx. USD 1,070–26,750) and possible closure order; persistent non-compliance can block licence renewal and prevent good-standing certification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a Luxembourg-approved réviseur d'entreprises is required if the SCSp exceeds two of the following thresholds for two consecutive years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average employees 50; audit is also required if the partnership is a regulated CRO, if all general partners are legal entities, or if the constitutive agreement expressly requires an audit. Otherwise the SCSp may rely on the small-company exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended law of 19 December 2002, implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted where applicable; CRO clinical-trial revenue recognition should follow the Luxembourg chart of accounts and, where IFRS is used, IFRS 15 principles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each SCSp must register in the Luxembourg RBE and file the initial UBO declaration identifying all direct and indirect beneficial owners. On every anniversary of registration, the general partner must file an annual confirmation of current UBO data. Any transfer of partnership interests, including changes in limited partners, must be declared within one month. The RBE confirmation is the primary annual register audit for the SCSp and must be reconciled with the on-site statutory registers at each anniversary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Limited and General Partners)
Register of Directors / Gérants (General Partner Managers)
Register of Transfers of Partnership Interests (where adopted)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000–2,500 per year for a Luxembourg City registered office and corporate agent address.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–18,000 for an unlisted SCSp CRO prepared under Luxembourg GAAP; USD 3,500–8,000 where a review or small-company exemption support is sufficient.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate in Luxembourg City (2025): 17% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% IP Box exemption on qualifying CRO proprietary technology income (effective ~5%); 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (>=10% holding, 12 months); multilateral group relief for intragroup loss transfer; unlimited tax loss carryforward under Art. 114 LIR

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 (Déclaration pour les sociétés de personnes) filed via eCDF electronic portal on MyGuichet (guichet.lu) with LuxTrust digital signature
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months of the SCSp's fiscal year-end (Art. 162 LGT); administrative practice grants extension to 31 December of the following year for calendar-year taxpayers; e-filing mandatory for professional taxpayers

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the SCSp reporting period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the same Luxembourg fiscal period used for the underlying commercial activity; non-resident partners align their foreign filing calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp name, RCS number, registered office, LEI
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use exact RCS (Luxembourg trade register) registration; non-resident partners must produce a local business identifier on schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income from CRO service contracts (clinical trial management fees) computed under LIR Art. 14
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to the Luxembourg PE; non-resident partners' share is derived by the statutory sharing ratio.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address, tax residence, share percentage and allocated profit/loss per partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach tax residence certificate of each non-resident partner; boxes support the MBT assessment only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit assessed to Luxembourg communal business tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: MBT is borne at the SCSp level; non-resident partners are not directly assessed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine up to EUR 5,000 and surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax (LGT Art. 176-180); late payment interest 0.6% per month; willful non-filing triggers criminal tax fraud prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (flat rate under LIR Art. 147-148; 0% effective for participating holdings >=10% held 12 months under Parent-Subsidiary Directive; no WHT on liquidation proceeds of a transparent SCSp because profits are allocated directly to partners)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply reduced treaty WHT: (1) obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the partner's state of residence (e.g., US Form 6166, UK form LUX/individual); (2) submit the TRC plus a beneficial ownership declaration to the Luxembourg paying agent / tax office before the distribution date; (3) for transparent SCSp structures, claim treaty benefits on a look-through basis: each partner must evidence treaty entitlement and substantive business/PE presence in Luxembourg; the ACD (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration) may request Form 2/5 or an equivalent residence certificate, a copy of the SCSp partnership agreement, and financial statements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Luxembourg WHT (no withholding on outbound IP royalties); Interest: 0% Luxembourg WHT (no withholding on outbound debt interest). Exception: 20% WHT applies to interest, royalties, or fees paid to entities resident in the EU/Luxembourg non-cooperative jurisdiction list (RDL, Grand-Ducal Regulation of 28 January 2021) when annual payments exceed EUR 100,000.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg (EUR): Local File required where annual related-party non-financial transactions exceed EUR 100,000, or financial transactions exceed EUR 50,000,000; Master File required where group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Report mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue >= EUR 750,000,000 (Grand-Ducal Regulation of 26 September 2018 implemented Action 13).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation, but substance requirements are enforced through: (i) GAAR and the abuse-of-law doctrine (Art. 6 LGT) denying treaty/ATAD benefits to artificial arrangements; (ii) PE threshold analysis under Art. 13 LIR requiring premises, personnel, and entrepreneurial risk in Luxembourg; (iii) the proportionality test for treaty access and Luxembourg tax residence certificates; (iv) the ATAD CFC and interest-limitation rules; and (v) the EU Unshell directive agenda — the SCSp must maintain real office, qualified CRO staff, service contracts, board/partner meeting records, and decision-making documentation in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful false declaration: booking fictitious CRO invoices, omission of milestone income, concealment of partner allocations, or sham contracts with foreign affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of undeclared profit plus 0.6% monthly late interest; administrative surcharge up to 10%; criminal fines up to five times the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years under the LGT criminal provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant (general partner/director) is jointly and severally liable for unpaid withheld taxes and fraud penalties; criminal conviction triggers asset seizure, travel bans, and professional disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp used purely as a conduit to channel CRO management fees to tax-advantaged jurisdictions without office, qualified trial managers, or local decision-making in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty/domestic benefits under abuse-of-law doctrine; retroactive reclassification of the SCSp as taxable under corporate tax (CIT + NWT); assessments extended to 10-year prescription; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 per false return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly certify false substance are personally liable for taxes, risk criminal prosecution for complicity in fraud, and may be prohibited from managing Luxembourg companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany CRO service fees without arm's length benchmarking, ex-post adjustments, or failure to produce Local/Master File documentation upon ACD request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary profit adjustment, recharacterization risk (fee converted into deemed dividend subject to WHT), late interest monthly, and mandatory penalties up to EUR 25,000 for documentation default.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing false TP policy documents incur personal criminal liability for aiding tax evasion; the ACD can pursue the directors of the Luxembourg payer for the unwithheld WHT.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion on Partner Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Passing dividends/profit shares to non-resident partners without applying 15% WHT or treaty reduction while failing to qualify for the parent-subsidiary exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SCSp is liable for the unpaid WHT plus 0.6% monthly late interest and penalties up to 10% of the withheld amount; for intentional evasion, criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant and resident managers are jointly and severally liable for the remittance of WHT; liability survives liquidation during the 10-year collection prescription.
